sections.content: **Scope note:** this repo has 300 test files; a full `bun test --coverage` run wasn't practical to include here, so I diff'd source against tests directly for the modules in your provided context (`Sketch.tsx`, `ResearchActivity.tsx`, `format.ts`, `ranking.ts`, `incident-format.ts`, `decisions-shared.ts`, `graph-visual.ts`, `FigmaEmbed.ts`). Say the word if you want me to kick off a full `bun test --coverage` run for a percentage-based report across the whole repo — that's a longer background job.

sections.title: Headline finding: this set is already very heavily tested — the real risk is duplication, not gaps
sections.content:
Every module I checked has **two independent test suites**: a flat `Component.test.ts` next to the source, and a second copy under `__tests__/Component.test.ts`, both re-deriving coverage for the same pure functions (in Sketch's case, 7 test files for one 489-line source file). This is almost certainly the parallel-lane protocol (`docs/planning/v13-proof-campaign-plan.md`) — two lanes independently wrote full suites for the same file without seeing each other's work. It's not wrong, but it doubles CI time and risks the two copies silently drifting once one gets updated and the other doesn't.

★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────
Coverage percentage tools reward this kind of duplication — 100% line coverage looks identical whether it comes from one thoughtful suite or five overlapping ones. The signal that actually matters is *branch* diversity: does any test exercise a code path the others miss? That's why I diffed source branches against test assertions directly instead of trusting a coverage number, which would have reported these files as "fully covered" while missing the three gaps below.
─────────────────────────────────────────────────

sections.title: Gap 1 (highest value): `briefAlignmentOf` — an entire tie-break dimension has zero coverage
Gap 2: `computeReducedMotion` — extracted "for testability," never tested directly
Gap 3: `barInsight` — the zero-base *downward* branch is untested
Lower-priority observations (not gaps, worth a glance)
sections.content:
- **Test duplication cleanup**: `src/components/cadence/{Sketch.test.ts, Sketch.test.tsx}` plus `__tests__/{Sketch.test.ts, sketch-helpers.test.ts, sketch-insight.test.ts}` all cover `mulberry32`/`seedOf`/`sketchPath`/`capFirst` near-identically. Same pattern for `ResearchActivity`, `format.ts`, `ranking.ts`, `decisions-shared.ts`. Worth a follow-up pass to pick one canonical suite per module and delete the rest — separate from this analysis and not something I'd do without your sign-off, since a delete here touches other lanes' work.
- Everything else I traced in `FigmaEmbed.ts`, `incident-format.ts`, and the `decisions-shared.ts`/`graph-visual.ts` record constants (`SOURCE_LABEL`, `STATUS_TONE`, `KIND_VISUAL`, `KIND_TRACE_PREFIX`) has direct, branch-complete coverage already — no action needed there.

Want me to wire the three skeletons above into the actual test files and run `bun test` to confirm they pass, or first run a full-repo `bun test --coverage` to get real percentages before deciding where else to look?

## Test coverage gap analysis

**Scope note:** this repo has 300 test files; a full `bun test --coverage` run wasn't practical to include here, so I diff'd source against tests directly for the modules in your provided context (`Sketch.tsx`, `ResearchActivity.tsx`, `format.ts`, `ranking.ts`, `incident-format.ts`, `decisions-shared.ts`, `graph-visual.ts`, `FigmaEmbed.ts`). ### Headline finding: this set is already very heavily tested — the real risk is duplication, not gaps

It's not wrong, but it doubles CI time and risks the two copies silently drifting once one gets updated and the other doesn't.

★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────
Coverage percentage tools reward this kind of duplication — 100% line coverage looks identical whether it comes from one thoughtful suite or five overlapping ones. The signal that actually matters is *branch* diversity: does any test exercise a code path the others miss? That's why I diffed source branches against test assertions directly instead of trusting a coverage number, which would have reported these files as "fully covered" while missing the three gaps below.
